Authenticate with API Keys
results.snippet:
Learn how to generate your Aircall API keys and use them to authenticate requests to the Aircall Public API. Before you start make sure you have the following:
- You must have an Aircall account. [Sign up here](https://aircall.io/get-started/) if you don't have one yet.
- An App or a tool for making API requests, such as curl, Postman, or your preferred HTTP client.
##
Get your API credentials
> **Never expose your API token in client-side code.**
> Anyone who can access it can make requests on your behalf.
> All requests to the Aircall Public API must use`https://`.
1. Open your Aircall Dashboard > Integrations > [API keys](https://dashboard.aircall.io/integrations/api-keys).
2. In the top right corner, click **Generate API key**.
3. Aircall will generate two strings: an `API ID`and an `API token`, which act as your username and password.
4. Copy and store both values somewhere safe. You will only be able to see the API token once — after closing the window it will no longer be accessible. If you lose them, you can always generate a new pair from the same page.

results.title: Aircall for Developers ﹣ Get started with Aircall OAuth
results.snippet:
The goal of the OAuth flow is to get an `access_token` that will be used to authenticate each request you will do to Aircall Public API. Admins will consent your app to access their Aircall data.
1. The flow is started when **Admins** install an app from the Aircall Dashboard. That's when Aircall redirects the Admin to your `install_uri`.
This step is often used to display a Settings page, instructions on how to use the app, any useful information for the Admin. Even it doesn't do anything specific, it must forward the user to `[POST] https://dashboard.aircall.io/oauth/authorize`.
2. Once redirected to Aircall, Admins will authorize your app to access their Aircall data. That's when Aircall redirects the Admin to your `redirect_uri`.
Use this step to get the OAuth authorization `code`.
3. Once redirected to your `redirect_uri`, you will need to exchange the OAuth authorization `code` for an `access_token`.
## Steps
1. Get your OAuth credentials
2. Setup a Web server
3. Implement the Install URI endpoint
4. Implement the Redirect URI endpoint
5. Retrieve a permanent `access_token`
6. Store the `access_token`
7. BONUS: automatically create a Webhook

results.title: Aircall API Authentication
results.snippet:
Aircall supports two ways to authenticate with the REST API: Basic Authentication and OAuth.
Use Basic Authentication when you are connecting your own internal tools or private integration to Aircall. Use OAuth when your app needs to access Aircall data on behalf of other users or customers.
| Use case | Basic Authentication | OAuth |
|---|---|---|
| Connect your own system and tools to Aircall | ✅ | ❌ |
| Build an integration for multiple Aircall users outside your organization | ❌ | ✅ |

##
Basic Authentication
Basic Authentication lets you authenticate requests with an `API ID` and `token` that you generate from your Aircall Dashboard.
To connect a tool or service, copy these credentials and paste them into the platform that you want to integrate with. This method does not require an authorization flow. Use Basic Authentication when you want to connect quickly without setting up OAuth.
####
When to use Basic Authentication
- You're connecting your own system or tool to Aircall
- You don't need to access data on behalf of other users
- You're building a private integration and are not an approved tech partner

| | |
|---|---|

Public App
A Public App is built to be distributed to multiple Aircall customers. To build one, you must first join the [Aircall Technology Partner Program](https://aircall.io/partners/technology/)
Public Apps are intended to be published and discoverable by Aircall's customer base. Public Apps use OAuth 2.0 so each customer can securely connect their own Aircall account to your integration.

Send your first authenticated request to list recent calls from your Aircall account. Use GET /v1/calls to verify your credentials and see the structure of a typical paginated API response.

Get your API credentials

4. Copy your `API ID` and `API Token`. You will only see the token once.

Make your first request
Choose your preferred method to send your first authenticated request.
1. Open your preferred terminal tool. Most common for defaults:
- macOS: `Cmd + Space` → Terminal
- Windows: `Win + R` → wt

```
curl -X GET

-u '<YOUR_API_ID>:<YOUR_API_TOKEN>'
```

results.title: Aircall Help Center | Using Aircall MCP with AI assistants (beta)
results.snippet:
**Aircall MCP** gives an AI assistant, like Claude or ChatGPT, read-only access to your company's calls and conversation intelligence data. Once connected, you can ask your assistant to search calls, pull transcripts and summaries, or check sentiment and action items, without writing any integration code.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI assistants to external systems. Where an API is written for developers to call, MCP is written for the assistant itself: it can discover what's available and use it without anyone writing integration code.

### How it works
1. You connect Aircall to your AI client once, via OAuth, the same way you'd connect any other app.
2. Aircall's MCP server publishes a catalog of tools it can use, such as "search calls," "get transcripts," and "get sentiment," each with a defined input and output.
3. You ask your assistant a question in plain language. The assistant reads the catalog, picks the right tool, and calls it.
4. Aircall returns structured data. The assistant reasons over it, or passes it to whatever you've built.

results.title: Register a Public MCP
results.snippet:
Registering an MCP with Aircall makes your tools and resources available to every Aircall AI customer, so it can call them directly instead of relying on a custom, hardcoded integration. The process has three steps on your side:
1. Build a compliant MCP.
2. Apply to the tech partner program.
3. Share the details we need to connect to it.

Prerequisites
- An MCP server reachable over HTTPS that implements the [Model Context Protocol specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io).
- You must be an approved technology partner or submit an application. Only technology partners can publish public integrations. See [how to publish an app](https://developer.aircall.io/docs/how-to-publish-an-app) for more information.
- Tools and resources with descriptive names, input schemas, and descriptions — this is what Aircall AI reasons over when deciding what to call.
- If your MCP requires authentication: an OAuth 2.1 authorization server, ideally with **Dynamic Client Registration (DCR)** support. Whether you support DCR determines what you'll provide in Step 3.

results.title: GitHub - growth-box/aircall-mcp: Local, read-only MCP server for the official Aircall REST API
results.snippet:
# aircall-mcp
A local, read-only [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for the official [Aircall REST API](https://developers.aircall.io/api-references).
Important
This is an independent open-source project. It is not built, maintained, or endorsed by Aircall.
## Why this server
Aircall provides an official REST API but does not provide a client-facing MCP server for reading calls and transcripts. `aircall-mcp` provides that MCP layer while keeping credentials and Aircall data on the local machine:
- **Read-only by construction:** only documented `GET` endpoints are implemented.
- **Local stdio transport:** no web server, hosted proxy, account, or subscription.
- **Fixed API origin:** credentials are sent only to `https://api.aircall.io`.
- **No persistence:** responses, transcripts, and contacts are not written to disk.
- **Bounded output:** pagination, compact call results, and transcript slicing limit context usage.
- **Sensitive media URLs omitted by default:** recording, voicemail, asset, and number-message URLs require explicit opt-in.
## Tools
All 21 tools are annotated as read-only, non-destructive, and idempotent.
